chunks.title: Frame ML expertise across model and production work
chunks.text: State the relevant ML domain, modeling stack, production responsibility, and one validated model or system outcome. Distinguish experimentation from deployed inference and monitoring. Avoid calling the candidate an AI expert based only on API usage or describing a prototype as production-grade without deployment evidence.

chunks.title: Separate modeling, data, and ML systems skills
chunks.text: Group skills into languages, data processing, modeling frameworks, evaluation methods, serving, experiment tracking, cloud, and MLOps. Include model families or techniques only when applied. This prevents Python, libraries, algorithms, and infrastructure from appearing as equivalent forms of proficiency.

chunks.title: Describe the complete ML project lifecycle
chunks.text: Cover the problem and dataset, preprocessing, baseline, model choice, validation design, relevant metric, error analysis, and serving or delivery path. State data size and split strategy where useful. A model name and accuracy score alone do not explain whether the experiment was valid or operationally useful.

chunks.title: Explain training and inference architecture separately
chunks.text: Describe how data is validated and transformed for training, how experiments and artifacts are tracked, and how the selected model reaches inference. Then identify serving mode, latency or batch constraints, monitoring, and retraining triggers if implemented. Do not imply an automated MLOps pipeline when steps were manual.

chunks.title: Report model improvement against a valid baseline
chunks.text: Weak: 'Built a highly accurate churn prediction model.' Strong: 'Trained a gradient-boosted churn classifier on 180,000 labeled accounts and raised validation PR-AUC from the logistic-regression baseline of 0.41 to 0.56 using a time-based split.' Name the dataset, baseline, metric, and validation design.

chunks.title: Use ML keywords at the right level of evidence
chunks.text: Relevant terms may include feature engineering, model evaluation, cross-validation, error analysis, data pipelines, experiment tracking, model serving, monitoring, drift, containers, cloud, NLP, computer vision, or recommendation systems. Select role-specific terms and tie them to datasets, experiments, or deployed components.
